evidence: interface.md Decomposition assigns non-money row-field normalization to Worker left, yet parseCsv only returns six strings and Primary also owns conversion into normalized records. This leaves date, currency, id, and category validation with overlapping or absent ownership. Smallest correction: make CSV syntax/column decoding exclusively Worker left and explicitly assign all incoming semantic field validation to Primary.

GOAL.md requires import to create an absent ledger, while interface.md exposes readLedger(path) without defining missing-file behavior. Returning [] would incorrectly make a missing report ledger appear empty; always throwing requires undocumented Primary handling. Smallest correction: specify that readLedger throws on ENOENT and Primary converts ENOENT to [] only for import.

GOAL.md defines repeated-ID skip/conflict semantics, but interface.md limits existing-ledger validation to record shape and does not define duplicate IDs already present in the JSON array. Such records can be double-counted by monthlyReport or conceal conflicting content. Smallest correction: require readLedger to reject duplicate IDs in existing ledgers before merge or reporting.
residual_risks: Until these contracts are clarified, independently correct Worker implementations can still disagree at Primary integration without editing overlapping paths.
